examples.en: My little brother scared me with a ghost story.

examples.ko: 아이한테 겁주지 말고 차분히 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't scare the child. Please explain calmly.
I said it to scare him, but he was really frightened.

examples.ko: 형이 큰 소리로 겁줘서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My older brother scared me with a loud voice and I was startled.
That dog scares people by barking.
There is no one you may scare as a joke.

explain: 상대가 겁먹게 만든다는 뜻으로, '겁먹다'와 짝이에요. '겁을 주다'처럼 띄어 쓰는 표현도 같이 써요. 활용은 '겁주어/겁줘'로 해요.

phrases.en: He scared me with a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겁주다'를 띄어 쓴 표현으로 뜻이 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of 겁주다 with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Please don't scare the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to do it.

phrases.en: I got scared when I saw the dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁을 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who gets scared.

explain_en: It pairs with '겁먹다' (to get scared), as it makes the other person scared. The spaced form '겁을 주다' is used too. It conjugates as '겁주어/겁줘'.

examples.en: The king gives an order to his servant.
The boss ordered us to finish the work quickly.
Do not give me orders.
I do not like the commanding tone.
The general will order the soldiers to move.
He gave the order and left.

explain: '시키다'가 일상에서 쓰는 말이라면 '명령하다'는 지위가 위인 사람이 강하게 시킬 때 써요. 군대, 왕, 법원 이야기에서 나오고 친구 사이에서는 좀 세게 들려요. 컴퓨터의 '명령어'도 같은 말이에요.

phrases.en: The general gives orders to the soldiers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명령하다'와 같은 뜻으로 명사 '명령'과 함께 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning as 명령하다, using the noun 명령.

phrases.en: Mom told me to clean my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명령하다'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 명령하다 and common in daily life.

phrases.en: The soldiers follow the order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명령을 듣는 쪽의 입장에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the one receiving the order.

explain_en: Give an order — authority figure to people (명령해요) The everyday word for telling someone to do something is milder; this one is a person of higher rank giving a strong order, as in military, royal or court contexts. Among friends it sounds harsh. Computer commands use the same root.

p.n: The replacement is stiff and literary, so odd in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 날씨와 판매량이 서로 상관한다는 연구가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a study showing that weather and sales are interrelated.
Don't butt into other people's business.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일에 상관하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to get involved in that matter.
I don't care who comes.
Why does my younger sibling interfere in my business?

examples.ko: 제가 뭘 하든 상관하지 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't interfere in whatever I do.

examples.ko: 친구가 그 일에 상관했다가 오히려 오해를 받았어요.
examples.en: My friend got involved in that matter and ended up being misunderstood.

explain: '상관하다'는 '~에 상관하다'처럼 일에 끼어들거나 신경 쓸 때 써요. 실제 대화에서는 '상관없다'(괜찮다, 관계없다)와 '상관하지 마세요'(참견하지 마세요)를 가장 많이 말해요. 뒤의 말은 조금 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I don't mind even if it rains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '괜찮다, 관계없다'는 뜻으로 일상에서 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday form, meaning 'I don't mind' or 'it doesn't matter'.

phrases.en: Please don't get involved in my business.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참견하지 마세요'라는 뜻이라 조금 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means 'don't interfere' and can sound a bit cold.

phrases.example: 나이와 상관없이 누구나 올 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Anyone can come regardless of age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 조건과 관계없이라는 뜻으로 자주 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase meaning 'regardless of' a condition.

explain_en: 상관하다 means to get involved in or care about something, as in '~에 상관하다'. In real conversation the most common forms are 상관없다 (it doesn't matter) and 상관하지 마세요 (don't butt in). The latter can sound a bit cold.

examples.en: Don't act greedy; let's share and eat.

examples.ko: 동화 속 욕심쟁이 할아버지가 벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: The greedy old man in the fairy tale was punished.
My younger sibling is greedy, so he hides snacks.
It feels bad to be called greedy.
Who might be the greedy one in our class?
That person is greedy but kind at heart.

explain: '겁쟁이', '멋쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙으면 그런 성격이나 습관이 있는 사람을 말해요. 가볍게 놀리는 말투라서 아이나 가까운 사이에서 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My child is a cute little greedy one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '욕심쟁이'와 거의 같고, 아이에게 귀엽게 놀릴 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 욕심쟁이, often used to tease a child affectionately.

phrases.en: Greedy people have few friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀리는 느낌 없이 중립적으로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral description without any teasing feel.

phrases.en: Taking it all for yourself seems greedy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 행동이 욕심 많아 보일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's behavior seems greedy.

explain_en: More neutral to critical; used for children and adults alike (욕심쟁이 사장님). Like '겁쟁이' (coward) and '멋쟁이' (stylish person), '-쟁이' labels a person with that trait or habit. It has a light, teasing tone, used with children or close friends. Using it for an adult can be rude.

t90.ax: It feels bad to be called greedy.

examples.en: My great-grandmother turned ninety this year.
On the holidays I bow to my great-grandmother.
My great-grandmother's house is near the sea.
My great-grandmother told me stories from her childhood.
My great-grandmother is in our family photo too.

examples.ko: 저는 증조할머니를 한 번밖에 못 만났어요.
examples.en: I could only meet my great-grandmother once.

explain: '증조할아버지'와 짝이에요. 어머니 쪽 증조할머니는 '외증조할머니'라고 구분하기도 해요. 높임 말이라서 '있어요' 대신 '계세요', '이/가' 대신 '께서', '에게' 대신 '께'를 써요.

phrases.en: My great-grandfather lived in his hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증조할머니'와 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pair of 'great-grandmother'.

phrases.en: My maternal great-grandmother is my mother's grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어머니 쪽 증조할머니를 구분해서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to specify the great-grandmother on your mother's side.

phrases.en: I go to my great-grandmother's house on Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집'의 높임말인 '댁'을 붙여서 어른의 집을 공손하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '댁' is the honorific for 'house', used politely for an elder's home.

explain_en: It pairs with '증조할아버지'. A great-grandmother on your mother's side is sometimes distinguished as '외증조할머니'. It is an honorific word, so use '계세요' instead of '있어요', '께서' instead of '이/가', and '께' instead of '에게'.

en: to advise; to give advice; to admonish

examples.en: I worry about my friend, so I advise honestly.
My teacher advised me to go to bed early.
I have one thing to say as advice to my junior.
The person giving advice isn't comfortable either.
He quietly gave his advice and left.
My older brother advised me, so I started exercising.

explain: '조언'은 도움이 되는 말이고, '충고'는 잘못을 고치라는 말에 더 가까워요. 그래서 윗사람에게 '충고할게요'라고 하면 건방지게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I listened well to my friend's advice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충고를 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the advice.

phrases.en: A senior gave me advice on how to study.
phrases.nuance_ko: '충고하다'보다 부드럽고 도움을 주는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 'chunggohada', with a helpful feel.

phrases.en: I advised him to fix his bad habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 위해 말해 준다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feel of speaking for the other person's sake.

explain_en: Frank advice about someone's faults; can sound blunt. '조언' is helpful advice, while '충고' leans toward telling someone to correct a fault. Saying '충고할게요' to a senior can sound presumptuous.

t90.ax: He quietly gave his advice and left.

examples.ko: 저는 교장실에 가 본 적이 한 번도 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실은 이 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The principal's office is at the end of the second-floor hallway.
The teacher took the documents to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실 앞에서 떨려서 한참 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous and stood in front of the principal's office for a long time.
Where is the principal's office?

examples.ko: 상을 받은 날 교장실에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the day I won the prize, we took a photo in the principal's office.

explain: 학교 교장 선생님의 방이에요. 선생님들이 모여 있는 곳은 '교무실'이라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.en: The teacher told me to go to the principal's office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교장실이 목적지일 때 '-로 가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -로 가다 when the principal's office is the destination.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the principal's office

phrases.en: I got called to the principal's office for fighting with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼나러 가는 느낌이 있어서 학생들이 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a feeling of going to be scolded, so students use it often.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called to the principal's office

phrases.en: The principal is in the principal's office now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교장실에 계신 분을 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to refer to the person in the office.

explain_en: The principal's own room at a school. It is the room of the school principal. It is easy to confuse with '교무실', the staff room where teachers gather.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 도둑질을 하면 안 된다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: As a child I learned that stealing is wrong.
Theft is a serious crime, so you get punished.

examples.ko: 가게에서 도둑질이 자주 일어나서 카메라를 달았어요.
examples.en: Thefts kept happening in the shop, so they installed a camera.

examples.ko: 도둑질로 잡혀 간 사람이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A person arrested for theft appeared on the news.
The villagers are anxious because of the thefts.
The punishment for theft is very strict.

explain: 행동은 '도둑질', 사람은 '도둑'이에요. 도둑에게 물건을 빼앗긴 쪽은 '도둑을 맞다', '도둑맞다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: You must not steal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 행동이라는 느낌이 강해요. '하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It strongly suggests a bad act, and goes with '하다'.

phrases.en: A thief came into the house last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도둑질을 하는 사람이에요. 행동은 '도둑질', 사람은 '도둑'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who steals; the act is 도둑질, the person is 도둑.

phrases.en: I had my wallet stolen on the subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 빼앗긴 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. '도둑을 맞다'라고 띄어 쓸 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the victim; you can also write it as '도둑을 맞다'.

explain_en: Stealing — the act itself, often with a moral judgment. The act is '도둑질' and the person is '도둑'. Someone whose things were taken by a thief says '도둑을 맞다' or '도둑맞다'.

t90.ax: The punishment for theft is very strict.

examples.en: Breathe in deeply and then breathe out slowly.
If you breathe in through your nose, you feel calmer.
The doctor told me to breathe in.
I feel good breathing in the clean air.
When you're nervous, try breathing in deeply.
Your belly comes out when you breathe in.

explain: 반대말 '내쉬다'와 짝으로 '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요'라고 말해요. 병원이나 운동할 때 많이 들어요. 공기뿐 아니라 물이나 음료를 마실 때는 '들이마시다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I breathe in slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숨'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이고 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 숨, in polite -요 form.

phrases.en: Breathe in deeply through your nose and out through your mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깊게'를 붙여 숨을 크게 쉬라고 안내할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 깊게 it is often used in instructions to breathe deeply.

phrases.en: There is a lot of smoke, so don't breathe in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형이라 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to warn someone not to inhale.

explain_en: To draw breath in specifically; everyday, used in instructions. It pairs with its opposite '내쉬다' in '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요', which you hear at clinics and in exercise classes. For drinking liquids, use '들이마시다' instead.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 허리 라인이 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: This outfit makes the waistline look nice.
I stand at the starting line and wait for the signal.

examples.ko: 회사에서 새 라인 제품을 곧 내놓을 거예요.
examples.en: The company will soon release a new product line.

examples.ko: 턱 라인이 깔끔해 보이는 머리 모양이에요.
examples.en: It's a hairstyle that makes the jawline look neat.

examples.ko: 이 라인 뒤에 한 줄로 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please line up in one row behind this line.

examples.ko: 그림에서 라인을 굵게 그리면 더 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: If you draw the lines thick in a picture, they stand out more.

explain: 줄, 선, 몸의 윤곽, 상품 종류까지 쓰임이 넓어요. '허리 라인', '턱 라인'처럼 몸 모양을 말할 때 자주 써요. 지하철 노선은 '2호선'처럼 '선'으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 헤어스타일은 얼굴 라인이 예뻐 보여요.
phrases.en: This hairstyle makes the outline of your face look pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴 모양의 선을 말해요. '턱 라인'처럼 몸 모양에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The outline of a face; 라인 is often used for body shape.

phrases.en: That company has a wide product line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 회사가 만드는 상품 종류를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the range of products a company makes.

phrases.example: 흰 옷에 파란 라인이 있어서 예뻐요.
phrases.en: The white clothes have a blue line, so they look pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 물건에 그려진 줄을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a stripe or line drawn on clothes or objects.

explain_en: Loanword for a drawn line or contour — design, art, body shape. It covers lines, outlines, body contours, and product ranges. It is common for body shape, as in 허리 라인 and 턱 라인. Subway routes are called by '선', as in 2호선.

p.n: 선 is the neutral everyday word; 라인 sounds like a design, sports or fashion line.

t90.ax: This outfit makes the waistline look nice.
